questions.question: Why do machine learning engineers save trained models?
options: To avoid retraining the model every time it is needed

questions.question: What does model serialization primarily do?
options: Converts a model into a storable format

A weather app predicting tomorrow's temperature

Which of the following is usually the FIRST step in a deployment workflow?

options: Models can become outdated or behave unexpectedly

Which statement about deployment workflows is TRUE?
options: Deployment includes monitoring and maintenance after release.
Deployment only applies to neural networks.
Deployment removes the need for evaluation.

Which scenario best illustrates model deployment?
options: A student experimenting with a model on their laptop only
A hospital using an AI model to assist doctors in real time

questions.question: Why is saving preprocessing steps along with a model important?
options: Because the model expects input data in the same format as during training
Because it increases the number of features

questions.question: A deployed fraud detection model starts performing poorly because new types of fraud appear. This problem is an example of:
Which order correctly represents a typical deployment workflow?
A company deploys a movie recommendation system. Millions of users receive predictions daily without retraining the model each time. Which combination of concepts makes this possible?
What is the primary purpose of an API in a machine learning system?
options: To allow applications to communicate with the model

In an ML API, the data sent by the user or application is called the:
The prediction returned by an ML API is called the:
Why are APIs important for deployed machine learning systems?
options: They eliminate the need for models.
They allow other applications to use the model's predictions.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an ML API?
options: A text file containing training data
A chatbot service that returns answers to user queries

questions.question: What is model monitoring?
options: Continuously observing how a deployed model performs

questions.question: Why is model monitoring necessary after deployment?
options: Because models may become outdated or perform poorly over time
Because deployed models automatically delete themselves

questions.question: A fraud detection model suddenly starts missing many new fraud patterns. Monitoring would help engineers:
options: Detect the performance drop and update the model

questions.question: Which metric would most likely be monitored in a deployed classification system?
If the distribution of real-world data changes significantly after deployment, the model may suffer from:
Which of the following best describes model versioning?
options: Keeping track of different versions of a model and their changes

questions.question: Why is versioning important in machine learning projects?
options: It allows engineers to compare, reproduce, and roll back models if needed.
It eliminates the need for monitoring.

questions.question: A company deploys Model v2, but users report problems. Because they kept Model v1, they can quickly switch back. This is an example of:
Which information is most useful to store along with a model version?
options: The office address of the engineers
Training data details, parameters, and performance metrics
The color of the computer used

questions.question: An online recommendation system uses an API to deliver predictions and monitoring tools to track click rates. This demonstrates:
Which scenario would MOST likely require creating a new model version?
options: Changing the model architecture and retraining it
Opening the dataset in a spreadsheet

questions.question: A customer sends an image to an AI service, and the server returns 'Cat'. The image is the ______ and 'Cat' is the ______.
What is the relationship between monitoring and versioning?
options: Monitoring can reveal problems that lead engineers to create a new model version.
Versioning eliminates the need for monitoring.

questions.question: Which sequence best represents a mature machine learning deployment lifecycle?
options: Train → Deploy through API → Monitor performance → Release improved versions
Monitor → Collect data → Stop the system

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of using Cloud AI services?
options: They provide computing resources and AI services on demand.
They eliminate the need for machine learning models.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes Cloud AI?
options: Running AI models only on personal laptops
Using internet-based servers to train or deploy AI systems
Storing models only on USB drives

questions.question: A startup uses cloud services to access powerful GPUs without purchasing expensive hardware. This demonstrates:
Why is cloud computing particularly useful for training large AI models?
options: It reduces the need for data.
It provides scalable computing resources when needed.

questions.question: Scalability in AI systems refers to the ability to:
options: Increase the number of features automatically
Handle increasing amounts of data or users efficiently

questions.question: An image-generation service suddenly receives ten times more users than usual. A scalable system should:
options: Add more computing resources to handle the demand

questions.question: Which situation best demonstrates scalability?
options: A system serves 100 users and cannot handle 101 users.
A system automatically increases resources during heavy traffic.
A model's accuracy increases after retraining.

questions.question: In AI deployment, performance often refers to:
options: How fast and efficiently the system produces predictions
The color of the user interface
The number of training examples only

questions.question: A chatbot that takes 20 seconds to answer each question has a problem with:
Latency in an AI system measures:
options: The time taken to respond to a request

questions.question: A recommendation system processes thousands of requests every second without slowing down. This indicates good:
What is a deployment tradeoff?
options: A method of deleting old models
A compromise between competing goals such as speed, cost, and accuracy
A way to improve every metric simultaneously

questions.question: A company chooses a smaller model because it responds much faster, even though its accuracy is slightly lower. This is an example of:
Which pair of objectives often conflicts in real-world AI deployment?
Why might a company avoid deploying its largest and most accurate model?
options: Large models may be too expensive or slow to serve.
Large models do not require training.

questions.question: A mobile app uses a smaller AI model directly on the phone instead of a huge cloud model. The likely reason is:
options: To reduce latency and resource requirements

questions.question: Which statement about cloud AI is TRUE?
options: Cloud AI always costs less than local computing in every situation.
Cloud AI provides flexible access to powerful computing resources.
Cloud AI eliminates the need for monitoring.
Cloud AI can only be used by large companies.

questions.question: A streaming service automatically allocates more servers during a major sports event and reduces them afterward. This is an example of:
An AI engineer must choose between a model with 99% accuracy that takes 10 seconds to respond and a model with 97% accuracy that responds in 0.1 seconds. This decision primarily involves:
Which sequence best represents building a high-quality cloud AI system?
options: Train → Deploy on cloud → Monitor scalability and performance → Optimize tradeoffs
